entries.name: Alice
entries.note: The young girl protagonist of Wonderland, the dreamer and main witness, present across all twelve divisions under varied aliases (the little girl, the child, the girl, Mary Ann by mistake); her sister is a separate person and is not in this group.

entries.name: Alice's sister
entries.note: Alice's unnamed older sister, who sits on the bank with a book, wakes Alice, and dreams of Wonderland; both entries describe the same individual.

entries.name: White Rabbit
aliases: the White Rabbit with pink eyes
entries.note: The one talking white rabbit with pink eyes and a waistcoat-pocket watch, who hurries Alice down the hole, owns the house, sends for gloves and a fan, and later serves as the court's herald and reader of the verses. All six entries are this same rabbit, so they stay together in this cluster.

entries.name: Dinah
entries.note: Alice's pet cat, mentioned only and never physically present in any division; all four entries (called the cat or our cat) describe the same animal at home, so they form one cluster.

entries.name: The riverbank
entries.note: The grassy bank beside which Alice sits with her sister, where the White Rabbit runs past and where her sister dreams at sunset; both entries describe this same bank, so they form one place.

entries.name: The rabbit-hole
aliases: the large rabbit-hole under the hedge
entries.note: A deep tunnel under the hedge that dips into a long, deep well lined with cupboards and shelves. Units 3-10.

entries.name: The long low hall
entries.note: The single long, low hall with a glass table and a small door behind a curtain, where Alice grows and shrinks; the three entries are different visits to the same hall, not separate places.

entries.name: The little door to the garden
aliases: The little door and passage to the garden
entries.note: The small fifteen-inch door in the hall that leads to a passage and the garden, locked with a little golden key on a glass table; both entries describe this same door, so they belong together.

entries.name: The Mouse
entries.note: The one mouse of the Pool of Tears who swims with Alice, is offended by talk of cats and dogs, lectures on English history, tells the long tale about Fury, and storms off; the same individual in both divisions, so no other mouse in this group needs separating.

entries.name: Ada
entries.note: A girl of Alice's age whom Alice considers as a possible identity in unit 10; not present.

entries.name: Mabel
entries.note: A girl of Alice's age whom Alice considers as a possible identity in units 10 and 13; not present.

entries.name: the Duck
entries.note: The one duck in the wet gathering of birds and animals, first in the Pool of Tears swim to shore and again in the Caucus-Race, where it questions the Mouse. Both entries describe the same duck.

entries.name: the Dodo
entries.note: The Dodo, a bird who is among those fallen into the pool, swims ashore with the party, and later proposes the Caucus-race, runs it, awards the prizes and presents Alice's thimble; both entries describe the same bird.

entries.name: the Lory
entries.note: The Lory, a bird from the caucus gathering who swims ashore from the pool and later argues with Alice about age and laments the Mouse leaving; both divisions describe the same bird.

entries.name: the Eaglet
entries.note: A young eaglet among the birds that fell into the Pool of Tears and gathered on the bank for the Caucus-Race; both entries describe this same bird, so they form one cluster.

entries.name: Pool creatures
aliases: the birds and animals that had fallen into it
entries.note: The crowd of birds and animals that fell into the pool and swim together to the shore in unit 26.

entries.name: the Duchess
entries.note: The short-tempered Duchess of the kitchen, who nurses the baby and sings the lullaby, later walks with Alice, is sent away by the Queen, and is named again as the imprisoned Duchess under sentence of execution; the Pool of Tears mention is the Rabbit hurrying to her. Only one Duchess appears in this work's divisions.

entries.name: Pool of Tears
aliases: the pool of tears which she had wept
entries.note: The body of water formed from Alice's tears, where Alice swims with the Mouse and the birds and animals swim; distinct from the shore, which is the bank.

entries.name: Shore
entries.note: The shore of the pool to which Alice leads the swimming party in unit 26.

entries.name: the old Magpie
entries.note: An old magpie who wraps itself up and leaves after Alice mentions cats.

entries.name: the Canary
entries.note: A canary who calls its children away to bed after Alice mentions cats.

entries.name: the old Crab (mother of the young Crab)
entries.note: The old Crab in the Caucus race who scolds her daughter about losing her temper; told apart from the Classics master by being the mother of the young Crab in the Caucus-race section.

entries.name: the young Crab
entries.note: A young crab, daughter of the old Crab, who snaps back at her mother.

entries.name: the assembled birds and animals
entries.note: The wet gathering on the bank who sit in a ring, race, and chorus their requests as one body.

entries.name: The bank of the pool of tears
aliases: the bank of the pool of tears
entries.note: The shore of the pool of tears where the wet party assembles, dries off, holds the Caucus-Race and the Mouse's tale, and where Alice is left alone; distinct from the opening riverbank.

entries.name: Mary Ann
entries.note: The Rabbit's housemaid, only named and never seen on stage; a separate person from Alice, whom the Rabbit confuses with her.

entries.name: Pat
entries.note: The Rabbit's gardener, an Irishman (speaks with an Irish dialect) who is outside the window and handles the arm; he is heard but not seen.

entries.name: Bill the Lizard
entries.note: Bill the Lizard, the lizard sent down the chimney by the Rabbit's servants and kicked out by Alice, who later serves as a juror at the trial and writes on a slate; the three entries are one individual across divisions.

entries.name: the two guinea-pigs
entries.note: A pair of guinea-pigs who serve the Rabbit, first holding up Bill outside the house and rushing at Alice, then cheering in court until the officers bag them; no note separates them from each other, so they are kept as one pair.

entries.name: the puppy
entries.note: A large puppy in the wood that Alice plays with using a stick.

entries.name: the Caterpillar
entries.note: The large blue, languid Caterpillar smoking a hookah on a mushroom, who advises Alice in the Caterpillar sections; both entries describe this same individual, the only Caterpillar in the group.

entries.name: the White Rabbit's house
entries.note: A neat little house with a brass plate on the door; Alice grows inside its tidy room, with the stairs and window.)

entries.name: the Rabbit's garden
entries.note: The area outside the Rabbit's house where Pat, Bill and the crowd of animals gather around the window and chimney.

entries.name: The thick wood (Alice's first wood)
entries.note: The wood where Alice wanders after escaping the crowd, meets the puppy and finds the mushroom; distinct from the mushroom clearing within it and from the Duchess's woods.

entries.name: the Pigeon
entries.note: An anxious mother Pigeon in a tree nest who mistakes Alice's long neck for a serpent's and accuses her of hunting eggs.

entries.name: Father William
entries.note: The old man in Alice's recited poem who stands on his head and balances an eel; he speaks with his son, the young man, in the verses.

entries.name: the young man
entries.note: The son of Father William in Alice's recited poem, who questions his father; exists only within the poem's verses.

entries.name: The mushroom clearing
aliases: the open place in the wood
entries.note: The open clearing where the Caterpillar sits on a large round mushroom and where Alice nibbles it; a specific spot, not the wood at large.

entries.name: the treetops
entries.note: The high tree where the Pigeon has its nest, among the trees under which Alice had been wandering.

entries.name: the open place with the little house
aliases: the little house in the open place
entries.note: An open place with a small house about four feet high, which Alice approaches once she has shrunk to nine inches.

entries.name: Fish-Footman
entries.note: A footman, so called by Alice from his face, who delivers the Queen's invitation to the Duchess at the door and then sits staring at the sky; not the Frog-Footman.

entries.name: Frog-Footman
aliases: the footman with a round face and frog-like eyes
entries.note: The footman with a round face and large eyes who opens the door and repeats the invitation message; sits on the ground outside afterward.

entries.name: The Duchess's cook
entries.note: The Duchess's kitchen cook with a pepper-box, who stirs peppery soup in the kitchen scene and is later questioned about the tarts before vanishing; both entries are the same cook, linked by the kitchen, the Duchess and the pepper-box.

entries.name: Baby
entries.note: The Duchess's infant, sneezing and howling, which Alice carries outside and which turns into a pig, then runs off into the wood.

entries.name: Cheshire Cat
entries.note: The grinning cat who talks with Alice, appearing in the Duchess's kitchen and in the trees or in the air over the croquet ground and vanishing; not Dinah, who is only mentioned.

entries.name: March Hare
entries.note: The one anthropomorphic mad hare of the work, first glimpsed at his large house, then a tea-party host, then a witness at the trial; all three entries are one recurring character, distinguished only by scene.

entries.name: The Hatter
entries.note: The Mad Hatter, host of the tea-party and later first witness at the Queen's trial; the Cat's mention of a hatter living the other way is the same man, so all three entries join one cluster.

entries.name: Queen of Hearts
entries.note: The short-tempered Queen of Hearts who orders executions, runs the croquet game and sits beside the King at the trial; all six entries (including the 'Queen' who sends the croquet invitation and the 'Queen' the Hatter recalls) are the same individual, so keep them together.

entries.name: Duchess's House
entries.note: A house standing in a wood, with a door opening into a smoky kitchen where the Duchess and cook are.Alice enters the kitchen here.

entries.name: The woods around the Duchess's house
entries.note: The woods by the Duchess's house where the footmen run out, the pig escapes and the Cheshire Cat sits in a tree; tied to the Duchess's residence.

entries.name: March Hare's House
entries.note: A large house with ear-shaped chimneys and a fur-thatched roof, where the March Hare is said to live; Alice approaches it at the end.

entries.name: the Dormouse
entries.note: The sleeping Dormouse of the Mad Tea-Party, who tells the treacle-well story and is seated between the Hare and the Hatter, and also the same Dormouse who sits beside Alice and is ordered out of court in the trial; both entries are one character, distinguished only by scene.

entries.name: Time
entries.note: Personified Time, with whom the Hatter has quarrelled; mentioned only and never present on stage.

entries.name: Elsie
entries.note: One of the three little sisters in the Dormouse's story, who lived at the bottom of a treacle-well; told of, not present.

entries.name: Lacie
entries.note: One of the three little sisters in the Dormouse's story, living in the treacle-well; told of, not present.

entries.name: Tillie
entries.note: One of the three little sisters in the Dormouse's story, living in the treacle-well; told of, not present.

entries.name: Tea-table under a tree
aliases: the table in front of the house
entries.note: A large table set out under a tree in front of a house, where the tea-party takes place.

entries.name: The wood after the tea-party
entries.note: The wood Alice picks her way through after leaving the March Hare's tea-party and before the tree-door to the garden; tied to the tea-party, not the Duchess's house.

entries.name: The garden
aliases: the garden entrance by the rose-tree
entries.note: The beautiful garden of flower-beds and fountains reached through the tree-door, including its entrance by the rose-tree where the card gardeners paint the roses; the entrance is part of this same garden, not a separate place.

entries.name: Two
entries.note: One of the three card gardeners painting roses red; the one who explains the mistake to Alice. Tell him apart by his role as the spokesman; he is a playing card, not a human.

entries.name: Five
entries.note: One of the three card gardeners; blames Seven for splashing paint and warns the others of the Queen's approach. Tell him apart by his blaming of Seven and his warning; he is a playing card.

entries.name: Seven
entries.note: One of the three card gardeners; blamed by Five and the one who checks himself on seeing Alice. Tell him apart by being the one blamed by Five; he is a playing card.

entries.name: King of Hearts
entries.note: The mild, timid husband of the Queen who pardons the condemned, tries to protect Alice, and sits as judge at the trial; told apart from the Queen by his gentle, merciful conduct.

entries.name: The Knave of Hearts
entries.note: The one playing card called the Knave of Hearts, who carries the King's crown in the procession, is tried for stealing the tarts, and appears as a cardboard figure in Alice's evidence dream; all three entries are the same individual across divisions.

entries.name: The Queen's playing-card soldiers
entries.note: The ten oblong card soldiers with clubs who march in the procession, form the croquet arches, carry out the Queen's orders, and appear as the court officers who suppress the guinea-pigs and remove the Dormouse; the same card-soldier retinue in each portrayal.

entries.name: the courtiers
entries.note: Ten diamond-decorated card courtiers who walk two by two in the procession.

entries.name: the royal children
entries.note: Ten heart-decorated children who skip hand in hand in the procession.

entries.name: the executioner
entries.note: The Queen's executioner who argues about beheading the Cat and runs to fetch the Duchess in unit 70.

entries.name: the flamingo
entries.note: A live flamingo used as Alice's mallet; it twists its neck and at one point flies off into a tree.

entries.name: the hedgehogs
entries.note: Live hedgehogs used as croquet balls, which roll away and fight one another.

entries.name: the Queen's croquet-ground
entries.note: The single walled-garden croquet ground of the Queen, with flamingo mallets and hedgehog balls, where the game and executions take place; both entries describe this same place.

entries.name: the Gryphon
entries.note: A single mythical Gryphon who guides Alice to the Mock Turtle, interrupts his story, and appears again in the court; the descriptions differ in wording but depict the same creature.

entries.name: the Mock Turtle
entries.note: A sorrowful, sobbing creature with a calf's head and a turtle's tail or flappers, who tells of his schooldays in the sea, the Lobster Quadrille and the whiting, and sings 'Beautiful Soup'; the two entries are the same character across divisions, distinguished from other names in the group only by being this single individual.

entries.name: the old Turtle master (Tortoise)
entries.note: The old Turtle who taught the Mock Turtle at school under the sea; only recalled in the Mock Turtle's story, not present on stage.

entries.name: the Drawling-master (old conger-eel)
entries.note: The old conger-eel who came once a week to teach Drawling, Stretching and Fainting in Coils; recalled in the Mock Turtle's story only.

entries.name: the Classics master (old crab)
entries.note: The old crab who taught the Gryphon the Classics, recalled only in the Mock Turtle's story and never present; kept apart from the Caucus-race Crab because the notes give no sign they are the same individual.

entries.name: the rock ledge by the sea
entries.note: The lonely rock ledge where the Mock Turtle sits sobbing and tells his story, near the sea.

entries.name: the undersea school
entries.note: The school under the sea attended by the Mock Turtle in his youth, existing only in his recollection; not shown on stage.

entries.name: Whiting
entries.note: A sea fish addressed in the Mock Turtle's song; it urges a snail to join the dance. Described as the subject of the song, not a physical presence on stage.

entries.name: Snail
entries.note: A snail in the Mock Turtle's song who refuses the whiting's invitation to join the dance, saying 'Too far, too far!'.

entries.name: Porpoise
entries.note: A porpoise in the song who treads on the whiting's tail; mentioned in the whiting's explanation and in the Mock Turtle's remark about fish needing a porpoise.

entries.name: Lobsters
entries.note: Sea creatures who serve as partners in the Lobster Quadrille; they are thrown out to sea and sing of their dance in the song.

entries.name: Sea-shore
entries.note: The undersea setting where the Lobster Quadrille would be danced along the shore and where the whiting and lobsters are placed.

entries.name: Court of Justice
aliases: the court of the Queen of Hearts
entries.note: The open court of the Queen of Hearts, with throne, jury-box and table of tarts, where the trial is held; the Lobster Quadrille entry is the same court heard in the distance before it is shown on stage.

entries.name: the jury
entries.note: The twelve jurors (birds and beasts writing on slates) who act together as one body in the court; both divisions describe the same jury, so the entries are joined.

entries.name: The pack of cards (the court's playing cards)
entries.note: The playing cards of the Queen's court who rise up and fly down at Alice, ending the dream; told apart from the jury by being playing cards in the dream rather than jurors in the trial.
